newsitem.title: USA: ATHLETICS-ALLEN JOHNSON EXPECTS RECORD BREAKING YEAR.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-ALLEN JOHNSON EXPECTS RECORD BREAKING YEAR.

text.p: After setting the Olympic record in the 110-meter hurdles last year, Allen Johnson has no intentions of slowing down this year.
"For 1997 I'm expecting to break the world record," Johnson told the weekly Track Writers Association luncheon in a tele-conference call Monday.
Colin Jackson of Britain set the world record of 12.91 seconds at the 1993 World Championships in Stuttgart.

"Last year my focus was the gold medal and I assumed that the world record would come along with the gold medal," said Johnson, who settled for a Olympic best of 12.95 in winning the gold medal at the Atlanta Games.

"The record will motivate me and it is something that every athlete shoots for and it is something I feel I'm capable of doing," said the 25-year-old Johnson, ranked the world's top hurdler last year after winning 11 races.
Johnson, though, is not about to slow down this indoor season either.
"I'm training to try to break the American record in the 60-meter hurdles this indoor season," Johnson said from Columbia, South Carolina, where he lives and trains.
Johnson will get his first chance to eclipse Greg Foster's record of 7.36 seconds at the 90th running of the celebrated Millrose Games at Madison Square Garden, Feb 7.
He will also run at next month's Grand Prix meet in Fairfax, Virginia and in both the U.S. National Championships in Atlanta and the World Indoor Championships in Paris in March.

Johnson will have to run fast to win for the second time in three years at the Millrose Gamsas. An accomplished field, including two-time Olympic champion Roger Kingdom, defending Millrose champion Courtney Hawkins and 1996 Olympic decathlon champion Dan O'Brien, has been assembled.
Last year Johnson lost the lead and a shoe when he clipped the fourth hurdle.
"It is always important to win, I feel it is important for me to win to get the season off on the right note," Johnson said. "This time my shoes will stay on."
Johnson is not worried about setting his sights so high for this year.
"I have the same attitude that I had when I was trying to become No. 1 and that is just go out and train as hard as I can," said Johnson.
"I don't feel any pressure at all," Johnson said. "It is just up to the other guys to see if they can catch me."
